title: Aqueous Extract of Freshwater Clam Increases Alcohol Metabolism in Rats
content: Excessive drinking or even alcoholism brings noticeable health risks to society, and how to improve alcohol metabolism may be a potential strategy to advance this public issue. The aim of this study was to explore the efficacy of freshwater clam aqueous extract (CE) in promoting alcohol metabolism and to further elucidate its potent mechanism. The male Wistar rats were divided into four groups: (1) Control group (C); (2) Vehicle group (V), which was given a single dose of 2 g/kg bw ethanol; (3) Low-dose CE group (CEL), which was given ethanol and 128 mg/ kg bw CE; (4) High-dose CE group (CEH), which was given ethanol and 256 mg/ kg bw CE. Blood was drawn from the tails of the rats at 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4 h after alcohol administration, and serum samples were collected. The results showed that compared with the V group, oral administration of CE reduced the ethanol concentration in the serum of rats, among which the CEH exhibited a significant difference (p&lt;0.05). Moreover, high-dose of CE (CEH) treatment significantly increased the activities of alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH), acetaldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH), catalase (CAT), and superoxide dismutase (SOD) in the liver of rats (p&lt;0.05). The results of western blot indicated that CE could reduce the expression of ethanol-induced inflammation-related proteins COX-2, iNOS and TNF-α in the liver. In conclusion, it can be inferred that the CE can effectively reduce the ethanol concentration in the serum of rats fed with alcohol, and its possible mechanism is to promote the metabolism of ethanol by increasing the activity of ADH and ALDH and antioxidant capacity in the liver.
